items.stem:

body font: house style Calibri 11 pt; document Calibri 9 pt

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain two advantages of using styles in a long document. (b) Explain why track changes is useful when several people edit a document.
items.answer: (a) Formatting is consistent; the whole document's formatting can be changed by editing the style once; heading styles allow an automatic table of contents and navigation pane. (b) Each edit is shown with who made it, so the author can review and accept or reject each change; nothing is lost and there is a record of changes.
items.markingKey: (a) 2 × (1 mark point, 1 mark explanation). [4] (b) 1 mark shows edits/who; 1 mark accept/reject or record. [2]

items.stem: Mei is writing a 60-page staff handbook for Palm Grove Hotel in Dhaka, which will be reviewed by several managers. (a) Explain how the table of contents can be produced automatically. (b) Explain how track changes would help the review process.

items.stem: BlueWave Supermarkets in Doha produces long technical manuals that are updated every few months. Evaluate the use of automated features such as styles, fields and an automatic table of contents in the documents of BlueWave Supermarkets.
items.answer: Points for: consistency; saves time; fewer errors; easy updates. Points against / limitations: staff need training; features can be misused (e.g. manual formatting breaks the TOC); setting up takes time. Conclusion: automation is very beneficial for long, frequently updated documents if staff are trained.

Conclusion may argue: automation is very beneficial for long, frequently updated documents if staff are trained. [6]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain what is meant by the term 'corporate branding'. (b) State what is meant by 'template'.
items.answer: (a) The use of a consistent name, logo, colour scheme and style across all of an organisation's materials so that it is easily recognised. (b) A pre-designed document or file containing the layout, styles and standard content, used as the starting point for new documents of the same type.

items.stem:
SwiftCar Rentals in Cairo has a house style. A report produced by Felix is checked against it:
heading font: house style Calibri 20 pt bold; document Calibri 20 pt bold
body font: house style Calibri 11 pt; document Courier 10 pt
line spacing: house style single; document single
logo: house style top left, 4 cm wide; document top right, 8 cm wide
margins: house style 2.5 cm left and right, 2 cm top and bottom; document 2.5 cm left and right, 2 cm top and bottom
Identify the features that do not follow the house style and state the correction needed for each.
items.answer: body font: change Courier 10 pt to Calibri 11 pt; logo: change top right, 8 cm wide to top left, 4 cm wide
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: body font should be Calibri 11 pt; logo should be top left, 4 cm wide. [2]

items.stem:

items.stem: Lotus Fashion in Riyadh has found that staff produce letters and reports that all look different. Evaluate whether Lotus Fashion should require all staff to use a strict house style.
items.answer: Points for: consistent professional image; brand recognition; saves time with templates. Points against / limitations: limits creativity; time to set up and enforce; some documents need different layouts. Conclusion: a house style with templates is beneficial, provided there is flexibility for special documents.

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'page break' and 'footer'.
items.answer: page break: A break that forces the text after it to start at the top of a new page. footer: An area at the bottom of each page used for repeated items such as page numbers, file name or date.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: page break correctly described; 1 mark: footer correctly described (a comparison is needed for full marks). [2]

items.stem: Explain the difference between 'page break' and 'header'.
items.answer: page break: A break that forces the text after it to start at the top of a new page. header: An area at the top of each page, inside the top margin, used for text such as the document title or logo that repeats on every page.
